subject: Franska
title: Grammar: present tense of -er verbs
sourceSummary: Present-tense conjugation of regular -er verbs, plus the irregular verbs être and avoir.

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "Je ___ français." (parler = to speak)
questions.opener: -er verbs in the present tense for "je" end in -e.
questions.explanation: "Parler" conjugates as: je parle, tu parles, il/elle parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils/elles parlent. "Je" gives "parle".

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "Nous ___ à Paris." (habiter = to live)
questions.opener: The present tense for "nous" ends in -ons.
questions.explanation: "Habiter" conjugates as: j'habite, tu habites, il/elle habite, nous habitons, vous habitez, ils/elles habitent. "Nous" gives "habitons".

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: "Ils ___ beaucoup à l'école." (an -er verb similar to apprendre: étudier = to study)
questions.opener: The present tense for "ils/elles" ends in -ent.
questions.explanation: "Étudier" conjugates as: j'étudie, tu étudies, il/elle étudie, nous étudions, vous étudiez, ils/elles étudient. "Ils" gives "étudient" — pronounced the same as the singular forms, but spelled with -ent.

questions.prompt: Choose the right verb: "Ma sœur ___ grande." (My sister is tall.)
questions.explanation: "Être" conjugates as: je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont. "Ma sœur" (she) gives "est".

questions.prompt: Choose the right verb: "J'___ un chien." (I have a dog.)
questions.opener: Avoir corresponds to English "to have". Before a vowel sound, "je" is shortened to "j'".
questions.explanation: "Avoir" conjugates as: j'ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont. "Je" (shortened to "j'" here) gives "ai".

questions.prompt: Write the French word for "you" (plural, several people you're talking to).
questions.opener: The same word is used both for polite "you" and for plural "you".

questions.prompt: Correct the two errors: "J'habites en Suède et tu parle anglais très bien."
questions.opener: Check which person each verb actually belongs to.
questions.answer: J'habite en Suède et tu parles anglais très bien.
steps: "J'habites" → "j'habite". The verb habiter is conjugated for "I" (je) as "habite", without an -s.
"Tu parle" → "tu parles". The verb parler is conjugated for "you" (tu) as "parles", with an -s.
Full sentence: "J'habite en Suède et tu parles anglais très bien." (I live in Sweden and you speak English very well.)

questions.prompt: How are -er verbs conjugated in the present tense, and how are être and avoir conjugated?
questions.opener: The most common verb group plus two of the most important irregular verbs.
questions.answer: -er (parler): je parle, tu parles, il/elle parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils/elles parlent. Être (to be): je suis, tu es, il/elle est, nous sommes, vous êtes, ils/elles sont. Avoir (to have): j'ai, tu as, il/elle a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont. Personal pronouns: je (j' before a vowel), tu, il/elle, nous, vous, ils/elles.
